summary: This work investigates surface post-processing strategies for aluminum superconducting resonators to preserve low dielectric losses during the 24-hour delays encountered in industrial multi-chip fabrication before cryogenic measurement. Selective oxide removal using HF vapor and phosphoric acid achieves the best performance, with median $\tilde{\delta}_\mathrm{TLS} = 3.6 \times 10^{-7}$ ($Q_\mathrm{TLS} \approx 2.8$ M) in the single-photon regime, while fluorine passivation, though effective at stabilizing Al against subsequent wet etch processes, increases loss by a factor of 2.4–2.9.
motivation: Industrial-scale superconducting qubit fabrication with multi-chip packaging and scheduling introduces delays between device preparation and cooldown, requiring surface treatments that maintain low dielectric loss under ambient exposure—a challenge not addressed by existing post-processing strategies developed for Nb and Ta resonators.
method: Three surface modification approaches were systematically evaluated on aluminum CPW resonators fabricated from a single 200 mm wafer: (1) oxygen plasma treatment (remote and direct), (2) fluorine passivation via CF$_4$ plasma following Ar ion milling, and (3) selective oxide removal with HF vapor and diluted phosphoric acid. Devices were characterized in a dilution refrigerator below 25 mK, with dielectric loss extracted via photon-number-dependent quality factor measurements.
result: Sequential application of HF vapor and phosphoric acid etching reduced low-power loss by a factor of three to $\tilde{\delta}_\mathrm{LP} = 5.7 \times 10^{-7}$ ($Q_\mathrm{LP} \approx 1.7$ M), with TLS-related losses of $\tilde{\delta}_\mathrm{TLS} = 3.6 \times 10^{-7}$, achieving the lowest reported $\delta_\mathrm{TLS}$ for the surface participation ratio and projecting $T_1 \approx 1.2$ ms for typical qubit geometries at 4 GHz.
